historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-case 10-year net revenue CAGR off the LTM mid-cycle base
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Trailing CAGRs are not usable as a growth anchor. They run trough-to-peak (FY2022 to FY2025) or pre-IPO-to-peak (FY2020 to FY2025); equity growth is dominated by share issuance (2021 listing, 11M shares for Deribit) and marked crypto gains; FY2022 EPS and owner FCF are negative so the 3-year figures are undefined. Peak-to-peak (FY2021 to FY2025) revenue CAGR is about -2%.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (OCF less other investing/capex, less SBC expense, less equity-award withholding tax, less corporate interest): FY2020 ~205, FY2022 deeply negative, FY2025 ~776, LTM Sep-2026 -342. SBC plus withholding tax was 49% of FY2022 revenue, 34% of FY2023, 16% of FY2024, 17% of FY2025 and 25% LTM: stock compensation is sticky in dollars while revenue is not, so owner FCF swings harder than reported FCF in both directions. Reported OCF also carries customer-related working-capital noise.

scenario_narratives.base: Crypto remains a boom-bust market and Coinbase remains its leading regulated US venue. Spot take rates keep compressing as volume shifts to institutions and derivatives (Deribit), which is why the last two cycle peaks produced the same revenue. Offsetting that, USDC balances and the Circle economics, staking, Coinbase One and the newer Everything Exchange products add a less volume-sensitive layer. Net revenue grows about 6% a year from a mid-cycle base, Adjusted EBITDA ex corporate interest settles at 33%, and stock compensation stays close to 1B a year, leaving an owner margin of roughly 20% at maturity.
scenario_narratives.bull: Stablecoin adoption under the GENIUS Act and a passed CLARITY Act bring institutional capital onshore; USDC balances on platform multiply; derivatives, equities and prediction markets make Coinbase a multi-asset broker rather than a crypto-cycle proxy; the Circle agreement holds on current terms. Revenue reaches ~15B by year 10 and operating leverage holds margins above 40%, with SBC falling below 10% of revenue as the May 2026 restructuring sticks.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 downturn deepens into a multi-year winter like 2022-23. MTUs and assets on platform keep shrinking, Binance, Kraken, Robinhood and traditional brokers compress consumer fees, falling short rates and a less favourable Circle split cut stablecoin revenue, and a security or regulatory event adds cost. Revenue falls to under 4B and recovers slowly, while stock compensation of 0.7-0.8B a year absorbs most of the operating profit. The marked value of the crypto treasury would also be lower in this case than the bridge assumes.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Valued as a cyclical operating exchange on mid-cycle owner cash flow, with stock compensation fully expensed and the share count held flat, corporate interest stripped from the flows and corporate cash, the crypto treasury and investments added in the bridge. Roughly a quarter to a third of value in the base case is balance-sheet assets rather than operations. The spread between scenarios is wide because operating leverage and dollar-sticky stock compensation amplify revenue swings; the house/street band is also wide because SBC runs at 12-18% of revenue.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle revenue is a judgment: LTM net revenue of ~5.3B is treated as close to mid-cycle. If the 2026 level is instead a new trough in a rising series, the base case is too low; if 2024-25 was the high-water mark for take rates, it is too high.

SBC treatment: the forward charge uses grant-value expense (17.8% of LTM net revenue). On the house historical basis of expense plus withholding tax it is 25.3%, and 2026 buybacks plus withholding of ~1.55B barely reduced the share count. Each 1pp of terminal SBC is worth roughly 3-4% of base value.
Crypto treasury (2.2B at 30 September) is marked at a volatile price and correlates with the operating scenarios: lower in the bear case, higher in the bull.
Circle/USDC economics: stablecoin revenue is ~1.2B a year, depends on short-term interest rates and on a single counterparty agreement.
Convertible notes are carried at 6.0B principal; a sharply higher share price would convert them into ~12.8M shares instead, partly offset by capped calls.
Adjusted EBITDA excludes the Data Theft Incident (over 350M in 2025) and restructuring; similar charges are likely to recur.
Acquisitions are not in the flows, and part of corporate cash is held against regulatory capital requirements.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 125.38-284.74
data_sources.financials: Q3-2026 Form 10-Q (balance sheet at 2026-09-30, nine-month cash flow statement, Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, cover-page share count at 2026-10-22); FY2025 Form 10-K; COIN_Metrics.csv and the kpis table

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted excluding note conversion: 264.76M Class A+B outstanding at 2026-10-22 (10-Q cover: 223.73M A + 41.03M B) plus ~11.4M treasury-method equity-award dilution (Q3-2026 diluted WASO 287.98M less basic 263.79M less 12.8M if-converted note shares). The convertible notes are carried as debt at full principal, so their conversion shares are NOT also counted. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: LTM to 2026-09-30. SBC expense 949.9 = 9M-2026 719.4 (10-Q cash flow statement) + Q4-2025 230.5 (FY2025 839.4 less 9M-2025 609.0). Taxes paid on net share settlement 397.4 = 9M-2026 303.4 + Q4-2025 94.0 (financing activities). Coinbase publishes no combined figure, so the historical owner-FCF base sums the two lines per the house rule. The FORWARD sbc_pct_path is anchored on the grant-value expense alone (17.8% of LTM net revenue): expense plus withholding tax double-counts the same awards going forward, and at the current share price vest-date value runs at or below grant value. On the summed basis LTM SBC is 25.3% of net revenue; that is the sensitivity to watch.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 11.0% in USD for all three scenarios: ~4.3% US 10-year risk-free, ~5% ERP, and a beta well above 1 for a crypto-volume-geared exchange, moderated by a capital structure whose debt is mostly near-zero-coupon convertibles. 50bp above the 10.5% USD tech house default. Cyclicality is priced in the scenario flows and weights, not in a further WACC premium or per-scenario WACC differences (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases, already expensed inside Adjusted EBITDA; lease liabilities (~$0.2B) excluded from net debt. One treatment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted, with the cyclical adaptations. Coinbase is an operating exchange/brokerage, not a deposit taker: customer custodial funds (4,462) and their matching liability are excluded from both sides, as are the lending book (loan receivables 1,976; crypto collateral and borrowings) and the short-term borrowings (749) that fund it, whose spread stays in operating revenue. FRAMING: mid-cycle, not peak and not trough. fy0 is the twelve months to 2026-09-30 so the flows start where the balance sheet stops (using FY2025 as fy0 would double-count nine months of 2026 cash already in the September balance sheet). LTM net revenue of ~5.3B sits close to the 2022-2026 five-year average (~4.8B) and well below the FY2021 and FY2025 cycle peaks (7.4B and 6.9B, which were roughly flat peak-to-peak despite bitcoin nearly doubling). The scenario paths are smoothed trajectories through future cycles, not forecasts of individual years. REVENUE BASE: net revenue, i.e. total revenue 5,629.8 LTM less Corporate interest and other income ~294.5, which is stripped because corporate cash is added in the bridge. The Q4-2025 component of that line is estimated at ~100 on the Q1-2026 reclassified presentation (corporate stablecoin yield moved into this line), so base_revenue is good to roughly +/-1%. EBITDA margins are company Adjusted EBITDA less that interest line, over net revenue: FY2022 about -14%, FY2023 27%, FY2024 49%, FY2025 ~36%, LTM 20.9%, Q3-2026 23.9%. Adjusted EBITDA excludes the Data Theft Incident and restructuring charges, which recur in some form; the margin paths are set a little below the adjusted history for that reason. NET CASH: cash and equivalents 8,603.8 (includes corporate USDC) less convertible and senior notes at 6,000 principal (carrying 5,947.8; fair value ~5,400). EQUITY BRIDGE: crypto held for investment, strategic and marketable investments are added because their gains and losses are excluded from the flows (matching-asset rule). BUYBACKS: 1,248.8 spent in 9M-2026 on 7.13M shares plus 303.4 of withholding tax reduced the basic count by only 3.1M, so the flat count is being funded but at a cost above the SBC expense at 2026 prices. NOT MODELLED: acquisitions (Deribit ~2.9B in 2025) as a recurring use of cash; regulatory capital that ties up part of the corporate cash; capped calls on the convertibles. PRICE: regular-session Friday close, not an after-hours print.

bear.narrative: A 2022-23 style winter followed by a weak recovery: net revenue troughs near 3.8B and is only ~5.6B in year 10. SBC stays sticky in dollars, so owner margins are negative for the first two years and settle near 12%.

base.narrative: Mid-cycle path. Year 1 runs near the Q3-2026 quarterly rate; recovery then compounds to ~9.3B by year 10 (5.8% CAGR). Margin recovers to 33%, below the FY2024 peak and around FY2025. SBC falls as a share of revenue mainly because revenue recovers, staying near 1B in dollars.

bull.narrative: The next cycle peak clears the last two. Net revenue reaches ~15B by year 10 (11% CAGR) with margins held near 42%, between FY2025 and the FY2024 peak.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: revenue is hostage to crypto prices, the company has just printed two loss-making quarters, customer metrics are falling 20-27% year on year, and the 2022-23 precedent shows how far owner cash flow can go negative when dollar SBC does not flex. Base 50%: the mid-cycle trajectory with continued fee compression is the central reading of two flat cycle peaks. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs several independent things to go right at once (legislation, stablecoin scale on current Circle terms, new asset classes gaining share, and cost discipline), though each is individually plausible.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
